author: Associated Press
description:
The measure comes as Canada imposes $20bn in retaliatory tariffs and Canadian prime minister Mark Carney vows to reduce his country’s economic dependence on the US

The US is banning dairy products, most alcoholic beverages and motorcycles from Canada, the White House said Tuesday, as the trade war between the two neighbors and longtime allies escalates.

The ban will take effect in three weeks and comes after Canada imposed retaliatory tariffs on $20bn in US imports earlier Tuesday.

Continue reading...
title: US bans Canadian dairy, alcohol and motorcycles as trade war with longtime ally escalates

author: Dani Anguiano
description:
Decision marks setback for president and Republicans, who set in motion national redistricting battle last year

The US supreme court turned back an emergency appeal by Missouri officials to use a newly drawn congressional map backed by Donald Trump in the November midterm election, letting stand a ruling by the state’s highest state court that blocked the new lines from taking effect.

Last week the Missouri supreme court ruled that the map must go before voters to approve or reject the new districts, meaning it cannot be used in the November election. Trump and Republicans fumed over the decision, with the president calling it “horrible, ridiculous, and unConstitutional”.

Continue reading...
title: US supreme court blocks Missouri’s new congressional map backed by Trump

author: Krishani Dhanji
description:
Follow the day’s news live

Migration fuelling almost half of regional growth

Migration is accounting for almost half of regional Australia’s population growth, a new report has revealed, as healthcare services warn of major workforce shortages if the intake is cut, AAP reports.

That’s democracy … if you’re in an election campaign and you make a promise as the local member, people expect that you’ll deliver on it. And that’s what this fund does.

title: Australia politics live: Victorian energy bills may rise by $100 a year under Coalition; Chalmers says One Nation would ‘destroy’ super

author: Dani Anguiano
description:
Officials say sighting a sign species – driven to extinction in state before reintroduction in 2011 – expanding its range

A gray wolf has recently been seen in California’s Mendocino national forest for the first time since the species returned to the state 15 years ago, state wildlife officials confirmed.

Officials in Lake county, which is about two hours north of San Francisco, said last week the California department of fish and wildlife (CDFW) had received reports of sightings in the forest in late August. The agency verified the presence of a wolf in the far north end of the county, county supervisor Brad Rasmussen said in a statement on social media.

Continue reading...
title: California hails rare sighting of gray wolf in Mendocino national forest

author: Associated Press
description:
Authorities accused Missy Woods of altering years worth of data in cases involving homicide, sexual assault and robbery

A judge sentenced a former forensic analyst for the Colorado Bureau of Investigation to 10 years in prison on Tuesday after authorities said her manipulation of DNA data had raised questions about the validity of hundreds of criminal cases.

Yvonne “Missy” Woods pleaded guilty in June to perjury, attempting to influence a public servant, forgery and committing a cybercrime. Dozens of other counts were dismissed as part of a plea agreement.

Continue reading...
title: Former lab analyst sentenced to 10 years in prison for manipulating DNA data

author: Victoria Bekiempis and Jeremy Barr
description:
Guy Campanile addresses ouster in Facebook post and says ‘we were told to leave because we insisted on doing our jobs’

The former managing editor at 60 Minutes, who was fired in May with several other top correspondents, has spoken out about the ouster, saying he and his colleagues, were dismissed because they “would not compromise our principles or reputations by jamming unverifiable notions or White House talking points into our reporting”.

Guy Campanile, who worked at CBS News for 34 years, said in a private Facebook post obtained by the Guardian on Tuesday that he had held off on commenting about his dismissal right away, having decided it was “wise to remain quiet when emotions are raw”.

Continue reading...
title: Ex-60 Minutes managing editor says fired staffers ‘refused to be accomplices’ in show’s ‘destruction’

author: Associated Press
description:
Brothers, convicted of parents’ killings and denied parole last year, permitted to apply for another hearing earlier than expected

Erik and Lyle Menendez will be before a parole board again in March, about 17 months earlier than expected.

The brothers were originally sentenced in 1996 to life in prison for the 1989 fatal shootings of their father, Jose Menendez, and mother, Kitty Menendez, in their Beverly Hills mansion. A Los Angeles judge reduced their sentences to 50 years to life in May 2025, making them eligible for parole because they were under age 26 when they committed their crimes.

Continue reading...
title: Erik and Lyle Menendez eligible to face parole board early next year

author: Heather Stewart Economics editor
description:
High yields threaten to wipe out at least half of the £24bn headroom John Healey was expecting to have for his budget

The UK government was forced to pay the highest interest rate for a 30-year bond since 1998 on Tuesday, underlining the fiscal challenges facing the chancellor, John Healey.

Echoing the global bond market sell-off that has driven up yields, or interest rates, on government borrowing across major markets, the Treasury paid 5.82% to borrow £4bn.

Continue reading...
title: UK government pays highest interest rate on 30-year bond since 1998

author: Zoe Wood and Rupert Jones
description:
Air traffic control issue affecting airports across UK on Tuesday has been resolved but disruption could continue into Wednesday

  • Flight disruption continues after air traffic control technical issue

  • Business live – latest updates

Airports across the UK including Manchester, Birmingham and all those in London were hit by problems at air traffic control on Tuesday.

The technical issue was announced shortly before 2pm and was resolved about three hours later. By that time, hundreds of flights had been cancelled, with knock-on disruption across Britain an
title: UK airport disruption: what are your rights if you have been affected?

author: Luke Harding in London and Amy Hawkins in Kharkiv
description:
Ruslan Kravchenko resigns over allegations some of his officials were engaged in large-scale money laundering

Ukraine’s prosecutor general has resigned after investigators used ladders to raid his office in connection with a major corruption scandal that threatens to embarrass Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

Ruslan Kravchenko quit his post on Monday after allegations that some of his officials were involved in large-scale money laundering. They received cash to protect call centres involved in illegal phone scams, it was claimed.

Continue reading...
title: Ukraine’s prosecutor general quits after anti-corruption agents raid his office

author: Peter Beaumont Senior international correspondent
description:
Several MPs also banned from Israel after UK steps up condemnation of settlements and announces sweeping sanctions

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Israel has ordered the closure of the British consulate in occupied East Jerusalem in response to sweeping UK sanctions on goods from illegal settlements.

Reacting to Ed Miliband’s description of violent Jewish settler activity on the occupied Palestinian West Bank as “ethnic cleansing” carried out with the tacit backing of the Netanyahu government, Israel’s foreign minister, Gideon Sa’ar, announced retaliatory measures including the closure of the consulate and entry bans on several UK MPs.
title: Israel to close British consulate in Jerusalem after sanctions announced

author: Tory Shepherd
description:
New research shows turbulent flushes create toilet-generated aerosols that can transmit legionella, influenza and norovirus

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Flushing toilets release particles into the “breathing zone” of adults and can remain suspended in the air for at least 20 seconds, a new study has found.

And closing the lid might not be enough to avoid a “plume” of potential pathogens.

Continue reading...
title: Flushing the toilet can release a ‘plume’ of breathable pathogens – and closing the lid won’t stop their escape

author: Jon Henley, Europe correspondent
description:
Bloc losing €13bn in revenue with one in 10 cigarettes illegal, watchdog reports

  • Europe live – latest updates

The illegal trade in tobacco is booming in the EU, according to a report by the bloc’s financial watchdog, with almost one in 10 cigarettes produced illicitly or smuggled, causing an estimated €13bn loss in tax revenue each year.

The European Court of Auditors (ECA) said in a report on Tuesday that the trade had “changed significantly” in recent years as smuggling, while still “a problem”, was overtaken by illicit manufacturing, which has increased dramatically in the bloc.

Continue reading...
title: Organised crime driving illicit cigarette factory boom ‘in almost every EU state’

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
The man, also accused of homophobic slurs on American Airlines flight, faces assault and disorderly conduct charges

An Arizona realty company says it is “no longer associated” with an agent who was recently arrested after alleged unruly behavior – including racist and homophobic slurs – on an airline flight led to his being zip-tied, duct-taped to his seat and arrested.

Layne Arthur Lundeen, 67, faces counts of disorderly conduct and second-degree assault in the case, according to Maryland court records filed after he was taken into custody at Baltimore’s airport on 3 September.

Continue reading...
title: US real estate agent duct-taped and zip-tied to plane seat after ‘racial slurs’ is fired

author: Chris Wiegand Stage editor
description:
Akram Khan among those paying tribute to ‘pioneering’ choreographer of intense musicality and grace who inspired generations of dancers

Sir Richard Alston, the British choreographer and teacher who took contemporary dance into new directions with his elegant and intelligent creations, has died at the age of 77. A former artistic director of Rambert and the Place, where he made more than 50 pieces for the Richard Alston Dance Company, he was celebrated for lucid, emotionally attuned work that was often as graceful as it was rigorous.

His death was announced on Monday by the Richard Alston Foundation, which was established in 2021 to promote contemporary dance and preserve his work. “It is with deep sadness that we have to report the death of Sir Richard Alston,” said the statement. “After a period of ill-health
title: Richard Alston, trailblazer and guiding light of British dance, dies aged 77

author: Tom Ambrose
description:
Voters will choose candidates across full slate of federal, state and local offices over next two days

Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

New Hampshire and Rhode Island primary voters will choose candidates across a full slate of federal, state and local offices over the next two days.

President Donald Trump said on Monday that ⁠Canadian private jet maker Bombardier would ⁠no longer be allowed ​to sell its planes in the United States unless it started manufacturing in the country. “NO MORE SELLING BOMBARDIER IN THE UNITED STATES! Their products aren’t good enough!” Trump said in a post on Truth Social. “If ⁠they want our Market, they must build here, and stop treating America like a ’piggybank’.”

New York mayor Zohran Mamdani is set to come face-to-face with Rudy Giuliani at the
title: New Hampshire and Rhode Island electorate to vote in state primaries - US politics live

author: Andrew Messenger
description:
Pre-inquest conference into Queensland deaths hears witnesses did not hear any smoke alarms during 2023 fire

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A landlord was repeatedly warned about improperly installed smoke alarms before a house fire that killed a father and five children in Queensland in 2023, a coroner has heard.

Deputy state coroner Donald MacKenzie held a pre-inquest conference into the Russell Island deaths on Tuesday.

Continue reading...
title: Mother flagged faulty smoke alarms before house fire that killed father and five children, court hears

author: Graeme Wearden
description:
Saudi authorities said operations at some energy facilities have been attacked ‌by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis

Gas prices are rising this morning, putting pressure on European countries who need to stock up their storage levels before the winter.

The month-ahead UK gas price is up around 1% at 184p a therm, close to yesterday’s highs when gas hit its highest since January 2023.

Continue reading...
title: Oil price approaches $100 a barrel after Saudi oil facilities attacked; UK mortgage rates highest since June – business live

author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
description:
Victorian One Nation leader tells media he has used methamphetamine, speed and marijuana

Victorian One Nation leader, Warren Pickering, has admitted he “made mistakes” in his 20s, including using ecstasy, methamphetamines and marijuana, losing his license multiple times for drink driving and hurting people he loved.

But he has denied claims by his ex-partner, published by The Australian, that he smoked ice in front of children and said he was considering legal action against the publication at a press conference on Tuesday. Guardian Australia and the ABC were barred from attending the press conference.

Continue reading...
title: One Nation’s Warren Pickering admits to illegal drug use and says he is ‘no angel’ in extraordinary press conference

author: Josh Taylor
description:
Even if the legislation passes, tech companies may still find ways to frustrate its intent and keep Australians hooked on their feed

Social media could become a “choose your own adventure” between the doom-scrolling status quo, or just the feed of the friends you want to see, if the government’s planned digital duty of care legislation passes, and the tech companies don’t muck around on compliance.

But that’s a big if.

Continue reading...
title: Social media users could opt out of the algorithm if Australian government has its way – but that’s a big if

author: Libby Brooks
description:
In today’s newsletter: The AfD’s local election triumph has shocked Europe, and raised questions about how to counter the rising far right

Good morning. Across Germany – and Europe more widely – there has been a palpable sense of shock and disbelief after the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) swept to a historic state election victory in the early hours of Monday.

It was, according to France’s European affairs minister, Benjamin Haddad, “a very grave moment for Europe”. The resonance was stark in the UK too: as the results came in, hundreds of black-clad activists intent on blocking migrant arrivals were battling with police for a second night along England’s south coast.

UK news | Batons and sy
title: Tuesday briefing: What happens next after Germany’s far-right breakthrough?

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Liberal MP says One Nation is trying to unseat him because he gave evidence against Victoria Cross recipient Ben Roberts-Smith

Andrew Hastie has threatened Pauline Hanson and One Nation strategist James Ashby with a “costly” fight over claims he is a traitor to Australia, labelling his critics “cowards” who don’t believe in the rule of law.

In some of the Liberal MP’s strongest comments yet about attacks from Hanson and her insurgent party, the Liberal MP said One Nation was trying to unseat him at the next election because he gave evidence against Victoria Cross recipient Ben Roberts-Smith in a failed defamation case against the Nine newspapers.

Continue reading...
title: Andrew Hastie threatens One Nation with ‘costly’ fight over claims he is a ‘traitor’ to Australia

Lawyers for an outlawed neo-Nazi political party have argued anti-hate laws passed after the Bondi terror attack rely on the opinion of a politician and are “authoritarian in nature”.

The White Australia party, formerly known as the National Socialist Network
title: Ban on neo-Nazi White Australia party is ‘authoritarian’ and breaches constitution, high court hears

A friend of Alan Jones who has denied witnessing an alleged assault in a Mosman restaurant has agreed in court that he sent the broadcaster a text message saying “if you need me to refute any lies, I of course will”.

Under cross-examination by prosecutor Georgina Wright, the witness agreed he was a loyal and “very good fri
title: Witness told Alan Jones he was ‘the greatest broadcaster ever’ while labelling SMH reporter a ‘bitch’

Barnaby Joyce, One Nation’s Treasury spokesperson, says his party has not modelled the potential impact on retirement incomes and inflation from his party’s plan to give millions of households early access to thei
